newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-BLANC CROWNS FINE 1996 WITH PLAYER OF YEAR AWARD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BLANC CROWNS FINE 1996 WITH PLAYER OF YEAR AWARD.

text.p: Laurent Blanc's comeback from a deep trough in his career two years ago was completed with his selection as France's 1996 Footballer of the Year.

Having won his place in Bobby Robson's multi-national Barcelona side after early difficulties this season, the France libero's only regret in a dazzling year was failing to lift the European championship with his country.
"As far as Euro 96 is concerned, I can tell you I've still got it there (in my throat)," Blanc said.
"The way we started out, we had everything to win that Euro or at least reach the final. We failed," he was quoted as saying by L'Equipe when he was voted his country's best player at the weekend.

Blanc, who makes telling sorties into attack playing for his country for whom he has netted 11 goals in 56 internationals, scored 68 in 265 French first division matches -- no mean rate for a defender.

The technically gifted one-time midfielder, criticised in the past in France for defensive frailities, established himself as one of the key players in Aime Jacquet's side preparing to host the 1998 World Cup finals.
Jacquet has known Blanc for years, having been his coach at Montpellier where he started his career in 1981 and stayed for 10 years, the first five in the second division.
"He's one of the leaders of the France team," Jacquet said. "When I was at Montpellier, I put him in central defence with (Brazilian) Julio Cesar."
But Blanc probably owes more to Auxerre's Guy Roux despite only one season under the wily coach of the reigning French champions.
Roux rescued Blanc from mediocrity when he signed the defender from struggling Saint-Etienne in 1995.
"He was the biggest star I've ever had in one of my teams," Roux said of a key player in the Auxerre side which completed the league and cup double last May.

"He completely fullfilled my dream of Laurent Blanc without my having to intervene. He scored important goals with his head. He became the best defender in the world and went forward at the exactly the right times."
Blanc's success at Auxerre ended years of poor choices of club.
His appearance in the French team from the late 1980s won him the first foreign transfer to Napoli after the Diego Maradona era.
But the move was not a great success as the club struggled to come to terms with life without their disgraced and departed Argentine idol.
Blanc returned to France in 1992 to play for Nimes for one season, then two at Saint-Etienne.

"There are players who have built incredible careers full of honours because of a good nose. Then, there are the performances on the field. At Nimes or Saint-Etienne, I had matches as good as those at Auxerre last season. But when you're in a lowly club, you're seen less," Blanc said.

"But I don't regret not staying at Napoli. Today, I'd still be in Italy and I wouldn't have known what I'm living at the moment," added the man referred to by Barcelona's fans as El Senor since he was signed last May.
